text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear position on self-driving cars","quality":"stance clarity","description":"It states a definite argument against the cars and keeps that position visible throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"one paragraph on cost, one on safety, one on liability","quality":"organization","description":"It is arranged into more distinct points, which makes the argument easier to follow."},{"evidence":"mentions the article’s driving functions, road changes, and camera monitoring","quality":"use of source details","description":"It brings in several specific ideas from the article to support the claims instead of relying mostly on personal opinion."},{"evidence":"asks who is to blame if someone dies","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"It raises the issue of responsibility in an accident, showing more awareness of a likely objection or complication."},{"evidence":"rhetorical questions throughout the body","quality":"persuasive emphasis","description":"It uses questions and emphasis to make the warning against driverless cars feel more forceful and argumentative."}]}
